skills.name: editable-export
skills.description: Give the person an editable copy of a video you made, built from its elements (footage clips, text, graphics, sounds, music), which opens in the EditAtlas studio, a web page with a timeline. There they fix small things themselves and export the MP4 again in their browser, without asking you to edit and re-render. Typical fixes are a sound that comes in a little late, text that sits slightly off, captions that are too small, a typo, a sound that is too loud, or a clip that runs a few frames long. You send the package as an encrypted link that expires after 30 days, or hand over the folder. The copy is optional. Offer it when you deliver a video, and build it only when they want it. Also use it when someone asks for "an editable version", "a project file", a "studio link", to "tweak it myself", "chỉnh lại chút", "tự sửa", "file để sửa", "chỉnh cỡ chữ", or "âm thanh bị trễ" after an edit. It is not a full editor; you cannot add new footage there or change effects that are burned into the clips.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+, FFmpeg with ffprobe, and network access to edit.trysometh.ing. render.py needs Playwright (pip install playwright) and Chrome or Edge. share.py needs the cryptography package. The studio needs Chrome or Edge 94+ (WebCodecs); Safari and Firefox are not tested. Works with the transcribe and sound-design skills.

skills.name: sound-design
skills.description: Sound-design a finished video with real sound effects from the EditAtlas library (2,278 described sounds, public, downloadable from GitHub with SHA-256 checks). Finds the moments in the picture, lets you look at them as frame sheets, picks sounds by description and measured numbers, places each on its exact frame at a level set by its role, keeps or replaces the film's own music and voice, renders a new MP4 plus a separate SFX WAV, and checks the result in numbers (sync, pace, holes, loudness, mono) before you show it. Use it whenever someone asks to add sound effects, SFX, whooshes, pops, clicks, hits, UI sounds or "sound design" to a video, reel, short, promo, motion graphic, product demo or talking-head edit; says a video "feels silent", "needs sound", "thêm hiệu ứng âm thanh", "lồng SFX", "thêm tiếng động"; or wants EditAtlas sounds placed on a video rather than just found. Not for composing music or generating sound.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, FFmpeg with ffprobe, and network access to raw.githubusercontent.com (or a local clone of EditAtlas/sfx). Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell.

skills.name: transcribe
skills.description: Transcribe the speech in a video or audio file on the person's own machine with Whisper (faster-whisper), with a time for every word, then check it, write SRT/VTT subtitles, and list what an edit could cut (long silences, filler words like um, uh, ờ, ừm, and repeated takes). The checked word-level transcript is what EditAtlas caption techniques, silence and filler removal, retake selection and every template's verified_transcript input need. Use it whenever someone wants a transcript, subtitles, captions or an SRT from a video; asks to "trích lời", "lấy lời thoại", "chuyển giọng nói thành chữ", "làm phụ đề", "làm sub", "cắt khoảng lặng", "bỏ ờ ừm", "speech to text", "Whisper"; or starts an EditAtlas edit that needs word times, even if they never say "transcript". Installs Whisper only after asking. Not for translating, cleaning up audio, separating a voice from music, or making a voice.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with faster-whisper (pip, about 300 MB on disk) and FFmpeg with ffprobe. The first run downloads a Whisper model from Hugging Face (0.5 to 1.6 GB); after that it works offline and no audio leaves the machine. Runs on CPU; an NVIDIA GPU is faster. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell.

skills.name: video-breakdown
skills.description: Break down a reference video shot by shot and name what it does, so the person can make one like it. Measures cuts and transitions (dissolve, dip, wipe, shape, iris, push, zoom, flash), camera moves (crash zoom, push in, shake, speed change), text and graphics coming on screen and their timing (in, hold, out), each text's colours (gradient stops, outline, glow) and free lookalike fonts, the look, pacing, the beat and sound hits; you look at the frame sheets, then look up each element in EditAtlas and write a report with technique names, links, sounds and a recipe. Use it when someone shares a video they like and asks what effect, transition or edit is in it, how it was made, or how to remake it; says "video này dùng hiệu ứng gì", "phân tích video mẫu", "làm sao để edit giống video này", "hiệu ứng chuyển cảnh này tên gì", "reverse engineer this edit", "what transition is this". Works on a local file. Not for downloading videos from TikTok or YouTube, telling filmed from AI footage, or editing the video itself.
skills.compatibility: Requires Python 3.9+ with numpy and Pillow, and FFmpeg with ffprobe. Runs offline; only the optional --check-api step, font lookalikes (downloaded once from Google Fonts) and the EditAtlas MCP use the network. Designed for Claude Code and other agents with a shell that can read images.
